candidate.title: ChIA-PET
candidate.scope: The single Illumina ChIA-PET schematic: protein-associated chromatin → Sample fragmentation → Immunoprecipitate → Ligation → Restriction enzyme digestion → DNA. The title expands ChIA-PET as chromatin interaction analysis by paired-end tag sequencing. Primary evidence resolves this as the original MmeI-based short-tag architecture within the broader ChIA-PET family. The first chromatin cartoon is an overview, not a separately evidenced preparation step. There is one depicted route and no alternative branch. The unshown long-read/advanced adaptation, Hi-C, HiChIP and ChIA-PET Tool software are not additional schematic targets. The graph ends at PET DNA; sequencing-library preparation and readout are explained only at their supported interface.

operations.label: Ligation
operations.description: Convert the two juxtaposed DNA fragments in the enriched complex into a physically connected DNA product at the orange junction while the protein-associated contact remains visible. The single broad caption covers linker attachment and proximity joining at this diagram’s level.
operations.mechanism: The original implementation attaches half-linkers containing MmeI sites to DNA fragments and then joins tethered fragments through linker-mediated proximity ligation. operations.information_effect: Encode proximity of the two DNA portions as a covalent DNA linkage. Inter-fragment ligation can carry a candidate chromatin contact, but the same assay also makes self-ligation and nonspecific inter-complex products. This one drawn route does not depict separate product-class branches.

operations.label: Restriction enzyme digestion
operations.description: Release a shortened junction-containing PET DNA product from the ligated material, separating the flanking DNA shown as detached strokes. The final arrow identifies the retained product as DNA, rather than depicting an additional named transformation. The schematic also collapses the transition from protein-associated material to protein-free DNA at this interface.
operations.mechanism: Primary-source resolution: cross-links are reversed and DNA is purified before MmeI digestion; protein loss is not attributed to restriction cleavage. MmeI sites supplied by the linker allow extraction of two short genomic tags with the central full linker retained. The final cartoon’s omission of the orange block is not interpreted as an extra linker-removal reaction.
operations.information_effect: Keep a paired genomic endpoint record on a tag–linker–tag DNA molecule while removing the longer flanks. Sequencing the two ends and mapping their genomic tags can locate the linked regions and support candidate protein-associated contacts. Self-ligated fragments instead inform protein-binding regions, and random ligation remains background; one paired molecule alone does not establish a specific biological contact. The figure does not depict sequencing or computation, and no alignment or contact-calling settings are introduced.
